title: Adic and rational smooth dualizing complexes
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, and let $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ be a
separated finite-type smooth morphism of pure dimension $d$. The
dualizing complex

$$
\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda
$$

has the canonical identification

$$
\omega_{X,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d]
$$

obtained by inverting the integral purity map of [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction]
when $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, and its transported purity map of
[thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] when $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$; the counit
identifies with the transported normalized integration map

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X(d)[2d])\longrightarrow\Lambda.
$$

proof.text: Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. The coefficient unit $U=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$ is derived complete and constructible, with reductions $U_n=(A_{E,n})_s$ in degree zero, by [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]. Each $U_n$ has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$: tensoring the free rank-one coefficient module with a sheaf $M$ gives $M$. Thus $U\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\mathcal O_E)$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Apply [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] to $f=a_X$ and $K=U$; its hypotheses hold because $X$ and $s$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $a_X$ is smooth separated of pure dimension $d\geq0$. Use the compatible integral purity family of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], whose reductions are precisely those of this theorem. The pullback formula of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] identifies $La_X^*U$ with $\mathcal O_{E,X}$: at each finite level pullback takes the coefficient unit to $(A_{E,n})_X$, and their derived inverse limit is the completed unit, by the same constant-coefficient lemma. Hence the purity map is $\gamma_{a_X,U}:\mathcal O_{E,X}(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_X^!U=\omega_{X,\mathcal O_E}$. Its inverse is the claimed identification. Here $\mathcal O_{E,X}$ means the completed coefficient unit, not the discrete constant sheaf.

source.place: first sentence: integral coefficient application and inversion of the purity map

proof.text: For $\Lambda=E$, use the image of $U$ as the lattice presentation of $\Lambda_s$; for $\Lambda=\Qlb$, use that $E$-object at a finite coefficient stage. These are the coefficient units specified by [def-pur-conventions] and [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]. Apply [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] to $a_X$ and these units. Its geometric hypotheses are those checked in Step 1 and its lattice hypothesis is supplied by $U$. The rationalized and common-stage pullback formulas of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] take the integral identification $La_X^*U\cong\mathcal O_{E,X}$ of Step 1 to $La_X^*\Lambda_s\cong\Lambda_X$. Thus it gives $\gamma_{a_X,\Lambda_s}:\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,\Lambda}$ at each of the two field stages. Invert this map to obtain the displayed dualizing-complex identification.

source.place: first sentence: rational and algebraically closed coefficient applications

proof.text: Write $\eta_\Lambda=\gamma_{a_X,\Lambda_s}^{-1}$ for the identification in Steps 1–2 and $\epsilon_\Lambda:Ra_{X!}\omega_{X,\Lambda}\to\Lambda_s$ for the counit in [def-pur-conventions]. Reading the counit through $\eta_\Lambda$ gives exactly the typed composite $Ra_{X!}(\Lambda_X(d)[2d])\xrightarrow{Ra_{X!}(\gamma_{a_X,\Lambda_s})}Ra_{X!}\omega_{X,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\epsilon_\Lambda}\Lambda_s$. At every finite level this is the smooth trace by [def-pur-smooth-trace]. The integral trace compatibility of [prop-pur-adic-reconstruction-trace-coherence] says that the composite at $\mathcal O_E$ is the adic transport of those finite-level composites; [prop-pur-rational-purity-trace-coherence] says that the composites at $E$ and $\Qlb$ are their rationalized and common-stage transports. To identify the normalization, use the affine-space clause of [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity] at each $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$: for $p_d:\mathbf A_k^d\to s$ its smooth trace is the product of the normalized affine-line traces and sends their ordered $d$-fold fundamental class to $1$. The current theorem explicitly identifies $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and assumes separated finite-type $k$-schemes; $\mathbf A_k^d$ and $s$ satisfy these hypotheses, and $p_d$ is smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$. Its coefficient-transport clause, together with the two trace-coherence statements just applied, transports this finite normalization along the same adic, rationalized and common-stage maps used in Steps 1–2. Thus the composite for $a_X$ is the transported normalized smooth trace; no fundamental class integrating to $1$ is claimed for an arbitrary $X$. Finally apply the point-fiber functor in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]: it sends the source to $R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X(d)[2d])$ and the target coefficient unit to $\Lambda$, giving precisely the asserted integration map.

source.place: second clause: counit, transported trace and normalization
